June 15th, 2026- Site updates, API, Beta, and Downtime!

5 months ago General


🏳️‍🌈💖Enjoy the site? Please consider supporting us via the links below!💖🏳️‍🌈

⭐ FA+ ⭐ SHOP ⭐ KO-FI ⭐Journal Start
Hey there Fuzzies!

It's been a while! Rednef has been having a lot of fun while I’ve been hard at work alongside the Tech staff. But fret not, we have a big juicy update for all of you!

Announcement Page New Notification Type (Modern only)



We’ve been posting updates and banners more often which means there’s been way more journal posts. As a result, we’re finding there are times where journal content would overlap and Rednef and I have to decide who gets to post. We don’t want to cut any announcement time short, so for these cases we are introducing the new announcement page and announcement notifications!



The new page includes all announcement journals by our mascots, Fender (Site and Tech Updates) and Rednef (Community Events and Spotlight). Announcement journals are sorted in chronological order and any you haven’t seen or marked as read will be highlighted. We hope this makes it easier for you all to keep up-to-date and easily see any journals you may have missed, including community events, site updates, and more! On our end, this means we don’t have to wait to share exciting things as they come up. We don't expect the number of announcements per month to increase, mind you. This just gives us the flexibility to share information with you in a more timely fashion without being confined to rigid schedules.

External Link Filtering



We all know that not everyone online plays nice. Unfortunately there are people who try to use Fur Affinity as a tool to take advantage of others. To address potential phishing and scam attempts via links, we've implemented a new intermediate page that will alert the user when they're leaving the Fur Affinity website. This will ideally cut down on accidental link clicks or situations where a scammer might try to mask the actual intent of their website.

We’ve also noticed some scammers sending notes impersonating staff. If you ever get a note that says it’s from Fur Affinity, verify that the person you're talking to is an actual Fur Affinity staff account before following any instructions! Staff accounts will have this shield icon before their name. We will NEVER ask you for your password or direct you off-site. If you encounter any suspicious activity, please open a Trouble Ticket to report it.

Comment Management (beta.furaffinity.net)



With recent adjustments to notifications and allowing for shouts to be hidden, we're adding the highly requested comment management page! This page will show ALL comments made by you, enabling you to delete or locate your comments at a glance. The comment management page is available for testing right now on the beta version of FA. You can access it via this link. Like other beta deployments, this is only available to FA+ members for testing at this time and it will go live for all users after testing is complete. If you want to give it a whirl before it’s officially released, sign up for FA+!

Bot and Third Party Activity


We understand that some people use bots and other third party software (such as art archivers, etc.) to interact with Fur Affinity. Due to the increase in traffic and the popularity of these solutions, we are updating our policy with regards to third party software. This section does NOT apply to individuals using software to interact with Fur Affinity in a more streamlined way like Postybirb and FABUI (these are not official Fur Affinity apps, but ones we currently permit).

We request that you follow these guidelines when using or developing third party bots and apps:
--Limit bot activity to periods with less than 15k users online.
--Keep your requests to once per second.
--Employ a proper exponential backoff scheme to mitigate overwhelming our services.
--During DDoS attacks, Cloudflare’s DDoS Mitigation may impact the use of third party software. We kindly ask that you do not use third party software while DDoS mitigation is underway.
--All third party apps interacting with Fur Affinity are the responsibility of their creators and are not supported in any way by the Fur Affinity Team. We will not take bug reports or handle issues with regard to how these tools interact with Fur Affinity.
--If your service interacts with Fur Affinity as a Machine-to-Machine service for the purposes of scraping or verification, we require that you seek permission to access our services by filing a Trouble Ticket in the Tech Category under “Access Requests” so we can identify your traffic pattern and ensure you retain access.
--We reserve the right at any time to revoke or block access based on perceived abuse patterns or unidentified, strenuous traffic. Please be respectful!

We’ve also received reports of users' scripts breaking as a result of Cloudflare blocks. We will be reaching out to those individuals who have submitted tickets to us shortly, and we apologize for the wait while we work on our internals to better support third party interactions in the future!

An Official Fur Affinity API and Closed Beta!



As part of the Developer Friendly Initiative, we will soon be releasing a consumer-facing API to interact with Fur Affinity programmatically. We will reach out to pre-selected individuals for testing soon, followed by an invite-only closed beta for interested parties, then a rolling release schedule from there. Anyone can apply to the API closed beta, and FA+ members will be able to join directly from the Discord once the beta goes live.

If you are interested in participating in the API closed beta when it is ready, please fill out this form: https://forms.gle/8XNUo61fK4VyQdHA6

We plan to offer a read-only API for the time being while we learn about the API’s impact on our database and begin tweaking to allow for writes in the future. We appreciate everyone’s understanding as we slowly implement new changes to a very old codebase!

Right now we are facilitating access to the API through Discord as a way to better collect feedback and let the community interact with the development team, but this will not be the case for the final release of the API! The final release of the API will allow you to interact with and register for the API directly through the site.

More changes!



Beyond these changes there are other smaller, but still important, adjustments to the website which you can view here.

Upcoming Downtime



We have a planned maintenance coming up for June 22, 2026 between 06:00:00 AM to 02:00:00 PM. This will allow us to make various improvements on our backend including upgrades to our database.

Thank you!


We have been very hard at work behind the scenes working on improving our Continuous Integration and Deployment Pipelines, as well as finally moving our version control to Git and creating reproducible environments for Fur Affinity. It’s been a lot of hard work from a small number of talented and dedicated community members that stepped up as staff, and we want to continue improving Fur Affinity for everyone. This also means that in the coming months, we’ll be able to begin supporting more developers and more volunteers as our codebase becomes more modernized and less fragile, so be on the lookout for recruitments! We are looking forward to working with the community and making something incredible together for everyone!

Reminder to keep comments on top and be excellent to each other!
Journal End🏳️‍🌈💖Enjoy the site? Please consider supporting us via the links below!💖🏳️‍🌈

Scrapers are never going to be fully stoppable, however, an open API makes scraping infinitely easier. There are specific API routes (retrieving your own account's data + acting as your own user for posting) that have genuine utility, but being able to search all posts that are by u_someartisthere really only has malicious uses. I do think sequential IDs is a horrendous design inherited from over a decade of neglect making scraping really easy. Obviously the internet is forever bla bla bla, but I've known Russian artists that have deleted their NSFW since it could get them in legal trouble that have to deal with archiver sites ignoring their copyright. I've also known artists that stopped posting (some on e621, some generally) because people were training LORAs on their art.

There will never be a perfect solution to these issues, I get that, dedicated people will find a way, but I still think artists need to be considered first and foremost when making these kinds of changes. A lot of artists left Twitter due to their works being easily consumed by Grok's AI edits, Bluesky never caught the same traction as Twitter, so if FA stops being friendly to artists, it doesn't matter how feature-packed the API is when all that's left is users, y'know?
kaisa @yuukari
fa tech manager 5 months ago
It depends on how you allow access to it! A lot of sites have an open door policy when it comes to API that directly allow consumers to use it without any proper vetting.

Our primary goal at the outset is to allow self-service for users to access specifically *their* data, like notifications and comments and feeds like that. While also allowing people to have a crack at a less restricted, but signup-required API for integration into services.

I'm eager to work with the developers in the closed beta to help shape this idea, but ultimately what I want to focus on is allowing the API to make interacting with FA better from a user's perspective by enabling people to make tools and interact with the site :3

Recalcitrantcalcitrant ~recalcitrantcalcitrant
5 months ago
If you're this worried about people training AI on your art, please use tools like Nightshade or Glaze that prevent them from learning anything. They do still work, and are very resistant to the image being squashed/stretched/compressed/converted/etc!


This cat and mouse game of restricting access out of fear is fundamentally more anti-artist, and the only way to achieve what you want is intrusive identity verification systems that would kill the site (while still not really stopping scraping)

Even YouTube, with all the resources at Google's disposal, could not prevent its anti-scraping measures from being totally defeated. This game is impossible to win, and every step just makes the site even more hostile to normal artists (many of which use tools like VPNs to protect ourselves from doxxing or being outed):


-Even without an API, people trying to 'archive' art can just right-click and hit 'save as', or write a program to do it automatically very fast.
-Disable the right click menu and they'll just use browser scripts to reenable it.
-Use JS to try detecting and blocking those and they'll just screenshot it.
-Use DRM to prevent that (like Netflix and other streaming sites do for certain content) and you'll lose half the userbase whose computers don't have a secure element set up to support that. Worse, many bad actors have leaked TPM keys that let them bypass this anyway.
-Use aggressive banning to squish users suspected of that, and they'll just make new accounts behind a VPN.
-Ban VPNs and they'll just use residential VPSes that are undetectable.
-Use ID based verification, they'll just use leaked IDs.

You can't stop criminals by adding more rules. And a hundred layers of DRM and identity verification before being able to use this site is far more "anti-artist" than a random nerd saving art they enjoy.
Jessamine ~bourbon.
Furry Artist 5 months ago
Glaze and Nightshade don't prevent genAI training. What they do is create a bunch of noise in the image so that the datasets are poisoned with it. Since genAI can't understand context, it feeds the noise into the datasets along with the art, increasing the chance of image muddying/errors. It ultimately doesn't do as much as people think it does because there's just too much data in the genAI datasets to combat at this point.

There's pretty much nothing you can do to entirely prevent what you post online from being scraped.
Recalcitrantcalcitrant ~recalcitrantcalcitrant
5 months ago
It is not noise actually! It's far more sophistocated than that. The modifications Nightshade provides are done with intention to make the image 'look like' entirely unrelated categories to other AI models, so that it classifies them wrong and thus screws up its feature encodings in the process.

Several studies have shown poisoned data like this causes massive model degredation even in small amounts. One artist using it is not going to wreck a model, but it certainly prevents them from gaining anything useful from that image.
Jessamine ~bourbon.
Furry Artist 5 months ago
It's basically noise. It's fancy noise, but it's still noise and doesn't stop the images from being scraped for AI. This has been known by artists since both came out, which is why there hasn't been widespread adaptation. It just makes your art uglier for no real benefit other than maybe damaging how the models work, but the models are already degrading anyways because of feedback looping from feeding off other AI data.
Recalcitrantcalcitrant ~recalcitrantcalcitrant

The reason why there hasn't been adoption is because it takes a lot of time and processing power to run, which is mildly annoying to do for every sketch, and because people don't understand that it's configurable: You can tone down the poison intensity to the point it's barely noticable to humans, but still incomprehensible to AIs.

It's also because many people think the fight is unwinnable. Disinformation like your post here doesn't help with that. If you have actual evidence it doesn't work, demonstrate it (and get a free ticket to publication in a major journal as a result).

It's fine to not understand how these tools work, but it's not fine to lie or spread FUD based on hear-say and anecdotes. There is no anti-scraping method OpenAI/Meta/Google/etc cannot bypass trivially, that is not a solution to protect anything.

zidders ~zidders
Anthro Artist 5 months ago
An API, or Application Programming Interface, is a set of rules and protocols that allows different software applications to communicate and share data with one another. Think of it as a digital translator or middleman. It takes a request from one system, delivers it to another, and brings the response back.

Take this restaurant example:
The Client (You): You sit at the table looking at the menu of available choices.

The Server (The Kitchen): This is the system that contains the ingredients and prepares your food.

The API (The Waiter): You cannot walk directly into the kitchen to talk to the chef. Instead, you give your order to the waiter. The waiter delivers it to the kitchen, retrieves the finished meal, and delivers it back to you.

softpaw ~softpaw
Photographer 5 months ago
It's an understandable triage response to an emergent threat; the amount of friction it imposes to users is pretty high, and while other platforms do implement similar measures, it's usually only on platforms that aren't primarily intended for public promotion or business communication, like Steam and Discord, so perhaps a longer-term compromise might be to set the filtering to only happen on links to untrusted domains/URLs, with the definition of "untrusted" kept fairly tight? That would keep the security benefits of external link speedbumps while also allowing frictionless traffic to external platforms where necessary. As for what would make the cut for "trusted" links, probably start with a handful of trusted domains that are also the most commonly used by artists trying to promote their business/work and where you can reasonably expect some level of moderation on the other end, like Patreon, Kofi, Paypal, SubscribeStar, maybe Bluesky, other art gallery sites (Weasyl, Inkbunny, DA, Flickr), maybe URL patterns that match the username-based profile contact link options, stuff like that. That would achieve the desired security guarantees long-term, while also alleviating most of the reasons people are likely to ask for an "off" switch.

Personally, I agree with the lack of an off switch for this URL filtering *if* it's applied in more limited and targeted manner, but the more blunt and exceptionless it is, the more people are gonna want to either turn it off or circumvent it by any means. Which can be counterproductive by incentivizing and normalizing URL obfuscation that's much harder to detect; for example, something Discord learned the hard way is that "copy this text and remove the spaces to go to it as a URL" *currently* looks so sketchy that most people on FA would never do it uncritically, but if sharing a link via normal means comes with so much friction that it feels "frowned upon", it drastically increases the odds of legitimate URLs getting shared in an obfuscated way, which makes "copy this text and turn it into a URL" less of a sketchy thing to do. One of my biggest frustrations as a security educator is that we've done a fantastic job of providing signals of *potential* risks in pretty much every context, but most people don't know how to assess the difference between potential risk and *actual* risk, so if someone's only experience with an alarm/signal is that they saw warnings that something bad might happen and it never did, that alarm/signal must not be that serious. A good example of this in practice is that most people take SSL certificate validation failure warnings pretty seriously, *unless* they work in an environment that relies on a private certificate authority without good root certificate distribution, OR they routinely work with systems on private networks using self-signed certificates, both of which make people uniquely susceptible to SSL-based attacks no matter how much technical knowledge they have, simply because it becomes normal to just breeze past the certificate failure warning in certain contexts.

So yeah, good and reasonable first step that's understandable under the circumstances, and I agree with other comments that having an off switch is counterproductive, but long-term, keeping it as blunt as it is is *also* counterproductive, so now that you've got the framework to make this happen in the first place, tightening the scope would be a great compromise to keep this useful and effective long-term :)

I love most of the things that this site is doing now, including the new Announcements Page, however, I do understand some of the points down here in the Comments, so, I'll give my opinion without sounding like an ABSOLUTE MANIAC like some of these folks, such as the harsh comments and unnecessary aggression.

If anything I said is not allowed, simply let me know and I'll edit it, such as the above "name calling", if you chose to see it that way!

Announcement Page

FANTASTIC Idea, I see no problems here.

Announcement Notifications

While I myself support this feature, I can ABSOLUTELY see why some people would see this as an annoyance, and they should be vocal about this, but they don't need to be dicks about it, that's my issue with their response. That said, I think an option to Opt-Out of the Announcements wouldn't be so bad, because if someone REALLY wants to figure out what is going one, they CAN go and look at the Announcement Page, so I don't feel that it's unrealistic to have an Opt-Out option for those that want it and have the notifications On by default.

External Link Filtering

This is a situation where I DO take issue with a feature, I personally have never liked websites that do this, Picarto off the top of my head, and again, just like with the Announcement Notifications, I think it would be nice to be able to Opt-Out of this, again, it's On by default.

There are many of us that are VERY careful with our online presence, what sites we go to, etc, and yes, websites like FurAffinity allow for Custom Linking, yes, like I just did (it's to FA's front page), and YES a fair amount of people click these blindly, or even non-custom links.

That said, for those of us that don't do that, we have the option to Mouse Over a Link (on Desktop) or press and hold on a link (on Mobile) and see where a link goes, and if we don't trust/know it, we don't go to it, or we look it up!

So yes, an option to Opt-Out of this feature would be very nice for those of use that don't need it, so for us it is only an annoyance.

Everything Else

I don't really have anymore to say about this announcement as the rest either doesn't apply to me, or is just a "wait and see" announcement, to which, yes, I will wait and see, lmao, so, for me, that is all!

Eden Vale @jamesalesto

The functional reason was that in the old system we had to carefully schedule announcement posts to both give users time to see and interact with the old one before the new one pushed it off.

This meant that information was delayed if we had numerous things going on. Effectively, we were constantly stepping on each other's toes.

Atm Tech is deep in the trenches on modernizing the codebase, so they have to work with the system as is to not side quest them from the overall task at hand too badly.

Eden Vale @jamesalesto
FA Ad Admin | Vampire Lover 5 months ago
Stack banners would inevitably have caused people to be upset that they've dismissed the banner and then it didn't truly dismiss. It's also still keeping the two sources of news separated meaning you'd have to go to either fender or rednef to catch up on updates vs a unified page.

It would also cause issues with our 3p advertising, which is a major source of funding for the site. They are notoriously picky about design elements that overlay ads, even temporarily.

Right now our codebase can only be worked on by a handful of people by nature of how it was set up 20 years ago. The Dev Friendly Initiative is a massive undertaking to not only modernize the code, but allow for more devs to come in and help.

The unfortunate and immediate result of this is our team can only work with the systems we have vs a massive overhaul and then they return back to the modernization efforts.

When it's only three people working very hard at a time we really don't want to distract them for too long. 😅

While we also can understand users want to customize their experience, the menus are in desperate need of an overhaul and adding more clutter to them now would be adding to the mess. Dev Friendly Initiative first, then we can consider more fun things.

The majority of people don't read banners, at all, it's called banner blindness.

If there is a way to turn it off, people are going to turn it off.

That's all okay until someone who turned it off is all of a sudden wondering why XYZ big change happened, not knowing that it had already been announced a number of times.

That user then comes to the newest announcement, and then complains about how sudden this was. They had no one to blame but themselves in this case.
There will be thousands of users like that. Not because they are idiots, but because they weren't informed. It's better to make that harder to happen in the first place.


Also, adding a toggle for every single interface change gets exponentially more difficult to manage. It's not at all feasible. this site already has a lot of technical debt from what I have heard, that would just make it worse.

Also, speaking as a nerodivrgent myself (and I assume you are as well, Hi!), it would depend heavily on the person but, almost all nerodivrgent people I know, would, not feel anything negative about this change, at all.

That way users can have a visual cue that a link is "good", and question where it goes and why it was linked when it does not "look safe".

It's especially good for those phishing notes people get. Since it halts the user's brain for a second. "Wait... why is an admin giving me a link that doesn't have a paw icon/have a yellow exlamation point? That seems strange."

gib ur cookies 2 fx now omnomomo 5 months ago
This would be extremely welcome (also yes, it would definitely need some kind of token) <3

I'll give my use-case - I use Postybirb to cross-post to a lot of different galleries. I also try really hard to be active and to monitor the galleries I post to. I've talked to critters before about what the barriers are for them to use more furry sites, and a common issue I hear is "artists upload art and never check their comments or messages."

Which is an understandable frustration, but if I'm uploading to probably around 7 galleries on average now, it is *very* hard to keep up with comments. And the way I've handled that is I scrape my notifications page (I think right now I send 1-2 requests once every 10-15 minutes). And then all of my notifications from every site get routed into one management system that I've built.

This works well, but it is a completely custom solution, it's kinda overkill in some ways - like I don't think I'm stressing the system but I also don't need the HTML, I'm just grabbing the notification IDs so I can dedup them and then saying "hey you got a comment on this piece, go to FA to check it."

If that was RSS it would be much much easier on my end. But also, I don't think I'm unique in needing a "Postybirb for notifications", I think I've just happened to be able to make a solution for myself. So FA adding RSS support for notifications would mean you could get comments and stuff just routed straight into an RSS reader without needing to code something special. I suspect it would be a really useful feature for artists.

And at least for me, being able to route my notifications into other systems leads to me being more engaged with the site and replying to more comments that my artwork receives.

We did add a new tag! You can see it on the help page. As for time zone stuff when JS is disabled, you can set what the server side uses via your account settings under "Time Zone". This is a fallback when everything else fails, so it might not be purrfect but close enough! x3

Akhlys ~leogarg
Watcher 5 months ago
That's awesome. But then there might be a slight issue. It displays 9AM-5PM for me, which is UTC. But in my profile, I set UTC+1 with daylight savings correction (so currently UTC+2). It should display 11-7.

gib ur cookies 2 fx now omnomomo 5 months ago
I'm still nervous about Cloudflare. So far FA has not been a problem, but more and more often I'm getting sent links to websites that Cloudflare just refuses to let me see - there's no fallback Captcha I complete, there's nothing but an endless spinner and a "send feedback" button that never gets seen - doesn't matter if I'm on or off VPN. There's no check to see if I'm not a robot, it just kinda.. decides "no".

It's difficult for me to overstress that Postybirb support is a requirement for me to post artwork to a gallery - I don't have time to manually upload pieces. And if Postybirb ever fully stops working on FA or becomes unreliable, there's just no way around me uploading fewer pieces.

Again, so far it has not been a problem.

I'm encouraged by the API developments, I'm really eagerly looking forward to them. I don't envy Furaffinity trying to figure out how to balance all of this stuff, it feels like the whole Internet is just getting worse. I can't offer advice on that, I don't have experience with trying to deal with scrapers.

But I'm dreading the day that things become so closed off that I have to start abandoning sites that I care about, and I'm dreading the direction that companies like Cloudflare and Google are taking their captchas. So even just hearing that FA is trying to balance this out, and is working on the API and is aware of the potential problems, does give me a little bit of encouragement.
